results.summary: This design implements a real-time audio transient shaper that independently controls the attack and sustain portions of an audio signal using dual envelope followers. It processes 6-bit digital audio input and produces 8-bit digital audio output, with control pins for attack and sustain amounts. The design operates entirely in the digital domain and requires external ADCs, DACs, and analog filters for practical audio use. It is a compact DSP block for audio effects, notable for its envelope modulation technique.

This project recreates the classic Mastermind game where players guess a secret combination of colors. It uses a random number generator to set the secret code and compares guesses to provide feedback on correct and half-correct positions. The game supports up to 16 turns and outputs hints via pins intended for seven-segment displays. It is a simple VHDL implementation of a puzzle game, best experienced with external displays.

This design implements a Morse code transmitter and receiver using two finite state machines to encode and decode Morse sequences for alphabets and digits. It accepts button inputs for dots, dashes, and spaces, and outputs decoded ASCII characters. The design is intended for testing with an FPGA board and a 16x2 LCD for display. It is a straightforward educational project for learning Morse code and FSM design.

This project translates Morse code input from push buttons into ASCII characters. It provides an 8-bit ASCII output that can be displayed on LEDs. The documentation is minimal, describing only the basic function and suggesting a test program. It is a simple VHDL design for Morse code decoding, but lacks detailed implementation or testing information.

This design is a Morse code transmitter and receiver with an additional serial receive input, implemented with two finite state machines. It encodes button inputs into Morse and decodes Morse sequences into ASCII characters. The design is intended for use with an FPGA board and a 16x2 LCD for output display. It is similar to a previous project but includes a serial RX pin for external Morse input.

This numerically controlled oscillator generates various waveforms including sine, cosine, triangular, square, and specialized shapes like Gaussian chirplet and ECG. It uses a phase accumulator and waveform lookup ROM to produce an 8-bit digital output, which can be converted to analog via an external R-2R ladder DAC. The design is tested in simulation or on hardware with an oscilloscope to observe the generated waveforms. It is a versatile DDS core for signal generation applications.

This project implements a numerically controlled oscillator with linear-interpolated sine output. It uses an 8-bit frequency control input and produces an 8-bit DAC output, with a 16-bit phase accumulator and sine ROM with interpolation. The design is a basic block for direct digital synthesis and requires an external 8-bit DAC and oscilloscope for testing. It is a compact and efficient NCO suitable for generating sine waves with controlled frequency.

This chip performs Manchester encoding and decoding, converting between parallel 8-bit data and serial bitstreams. It includes a built-in 5x PLL and supports bidirectional operation controlled by a direction pin, with additional features like BIST mode and debug outputs. The design requires two clock inputs (25MHz and 100MHz) and uses bidirectional pins for data. Silicon testing confirmed functionality, with successful loopback tests using an external CPLD.

This project is a write-only I2C slave with address 0x8E, featuring three control registers and eight data registers. It supports direct passthrough mode and a stepper mode that sequentially activates outputs based on a programmable counter. The design requires an external I2C master, switches for inputs, and LEDs or a seven-segment display for outputs. It is a configurable I2C peripheral for controlling external devices.

This design is a standalone GPU that performs transformation, lighting, and rasterization to render 3D models from QSPI flash memory. It outputs VGA signals with 4-bit color and supports double buffering and z-buffering, achieving 6.5 fps for 1K triangles at 320x240 resolution. It interfaces with a gamepad for interactive control and uses QSPI RAM for frame buffers. Silicon testing confirmed it works as expected, making it a notable compact 3D graphics accelerator.
